manifest.title: SDOH Loop Mapper: map a person's or group's social circumstances with ICD-11 codes and find the loops that hold them in place
manifest.question: How do the social determinants of a person's or group's health, well-being and livelihood — named with ICD-11's codes — feed one another, and which reinforcing and balancing loops hold their situation in place?

permissions.text: builder-authored; ICD-11 titles and definitions reproduced verbatim from the WHO ICD-API with code, title and URI (WHO, CC BY-ND 3.0 IGO, ICD-11 licence checked 2026-11-02; crosswalk use under §1.2.4 is undecided, todo T-LIC-01); abstracts verbatim with source; no other third-party text beyond quotations of 25 words or fewer

personas.label: A navigator or community health worker mapping a client's situation
personas.situation: Meets a client whose problems — rent, work, a partner, a child's school — keep feeding each other.
personas.deciding: Which circumstances to tackle first, and how to explain the knot to a supervisor or a referral partner.
jobs: Turn what the client told me into a map I can show someone else
See which problems sit inside the same loop, so one fix might ease several
Code each circumstance the way the health system will recognise it

personas.label: A student or researcher learning SDOH and causal loop diagrams
personas.situation: Studies social determinants and wants to model how they interact for a population or a case.
personas.deciding: How to represent the causal structure, and which links are backed by evidence.
jobs: Find the seminal research behind each social determinant
Build a causal loop diagram and list its reinforcing and balancing loops
Weight the links and export the map and a loop report for a paper or class

personas.label: A family caregiver trying to make sense of a relative's situation
personas.situation: Helping a parent or sibling whose money, housing and health problems feel like one tangle.
personas.deciding: What is driving what, and what to raise with a social worker or navigator.
jobs: Write down what is going on without having to know the codes
Show a navigator a simple picture of how things connect

safety.notice: This is a thinking tool for mapping how a person's or a group's social circumstances connect. It describes circumstances using codes from the World Health Organization's ICD-11; it does not diagnose anyone, give medical, legal or financial advice, or replace a professional who knows the situation. Everything you type stays in this browser on this device unless you export it.

deidentify.nudge: Use initials or a label. Don't enter names, dates of birth, addresses or record numbers.

interview.a: Interim mirror (option A); each pop-out links the WHO entry; WHO ICD-API before any wider release

in: ICD-11 MMS Chapter 24 blocks QD50–QE9Z (the SDOH set); QF20–QF2Z carried as 'functioning', outside the SDOH set
Seminal frameworks (WHO CSDH, Solar–Irwin), the social gradient and fundamental-cause literature
Domain evidence for associations between the ICD-11 blocks, graded S/M/F
Causal-loop and fuzzy-cognitive-map methods for the analyses
out: Clinical diagnosis and treatment (health safety profile)
Local services and resources (resources module off in the pilot)
Quantitative effect sizes as edge weights — weights are the user's judgement

search_strategy.approach: Seeded from the seminal SDOH literature known to the builder, then every DOI verified one at a time against OpenAlex and Crossref (sequential, paced) and abstracts harvested verbatim by tools/harvest_openalex.py on Daniel's machine, with Europe PMC as the fallback. ICD-11 codes first extracted block by block from the findacode.com mirror of release 2026-01, then replaced on 2026-11-02 by WHO's own text from the WHO ICD-API. Framework pages (WHO, ODPHP, CMS) read directly. This is a scope-bounded commissioned research pack, not a systematic review.
known_gaps: No systematic search with hit counts; the corpus is curated, not exhaustive
Links are block-level; code-level evidence is suggested, not established
Evidence is mostly from the United States and the United Kingdom

todo.status: checked 2026-11-02 against WHO's ICD-11 Terms of Use and License Agreement (icd.who.int/en/docs/ICD11-license.pdf): CC BY-ND 3.0 IGO. Software may incorporate ICD-11 and carry code, title and URI (§1.2.2–1.2.3; 125/126 codes have a URI, QD71.Z links to the browser root). Added data fields are allowed if clearly marked as not from WHO (§1.2.5; the builder's tiers and links are labelled). Required: the citation 'International Classification of Diseases, Eleventh Revision (ICD-11), World Health Organization (WHO) 2019 https://icd.who.int/browse11. Licensed under CC BY-ND 3.0 IGO' (§1.3) — not yet shown in the app. No WHO name or emblem as endorsement (§4.1). DECIDED 2026-11-02 (Daniel): keep the crosswalk while the app stays local; Daniel wants the app public within 2–3 weeks (by about 2026-11-20). WHO permissions request submitted 2026-11-02 (request ID 202611431). Plan: wait for WHO's written agreement; if none by about 2026-11-16, ship with the ICD-10-CM line removed and the HP2030 domains kept as a builder topic tag. Background: §1.2.4 says mapping or crosswalks between ICD-11 and other classifications need a separate written agreement from WHO, and the app ships a proposed ICD-10-CM / HP2030 crosswalk (114 codes). Not legal advice.
